_comment: SESSION 27 -- THE BUTTON IS ABSENT AND THE RULE TABLE SAYS YES. This is fixture 5's board with
ONE change: the Eldrazi Displacer is in HAND instead of on the battlefield. Everything else is
identical -- same lands, same Peregrine Drake, same deployed Dimensional Infiltrator, same
`ComboOffPossible` answers this board YES, rule DEPLOYED: RecogniseFlickerLoopProspective picks
the outlet out of hand (MTG_COMBO_OFF_PROSPECTIVE), the Drake untaps five, and the loop funds
the Infiltrator's twelve exiles. The BUTTON is nevertheless absent, and the reason is upstream of
every row of the table: `EnumerateMainPlans` consults it only behind `best_any >= 0` -- some
enumerated plan must already carry an `ActivateBlink` with `chosen_x > 3` -- and an ActivateBlink
needs the outlet ALREADY on the battlefield. A plan that casts the outlet and then goes off in
the same plan is not expressible, so no candidate carries a go-off, so nothing asks the rule.
WHY THIS IS PINNED. Session 27 measured the sweep's autonomous MISSED FIREs and every one of the
twelve was this shape: consulted=0 on all 12, and the rule would have FIRED on 9. Counting them
as 'the rule is too tight' pointed the next fixer at a table that is already right. The three
assertions below say exactly which half is which, and they guard in BOTH directions: narrow the
table and `expect_rule_says` fails; give the enumerator a cast-then-go-off plan (or relax the
precondition) and `expect_rule_consulted` fails -- at which point this fixture should be
re-authored to expect the button, because the button would then be RIGHT.
The positive control is edf_co_34: the same board with the outlet back in play.
